notes:
-- Background: mid-stage cloud-native finance firm (payment settlement infra). Evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) for latency-sensitive chat + rerank pipelines. Primary driver: keep PII and transaction metadata in EU-only tenancy and maintain strict audit trail.

-- From security call (02/03/2026, CISO + infra): 'we need static egress or PrivateLink — can't rely on broad NAT egress for allowlists.' CISO asked for design options: AWS PrivateLink vs VPC peering vs Transit Gateway.

-- Technical constraints / asks (explicit):
  * Support for AWS PrivateLink endpoints into Redwood control plane (customerside interface) OR documented VPC peering architecture with route table examples.
  * Static egress IP ranges or predictable egress via customer-managed NAT/egress proxy so downstream partners can IP-allowlist.
  * Detailed firewall/security-group guidance: examples for minimal inbound ports, explicit TLS/mTLS port list, recommended SG rules for LB->workers.
  * Egress controls: ability to restrict outbound traffic to Redwood endpoints only (no general internet egress).
  * KMS/BYOK: require customer-managed keys in AWS KMS (or CloudHSM backing) with audit events surfaced to their SIEM. Key rotation policy must be configurable.
  * Audit logging: native forwarding of request & token-level audit to S3 (EU bucket) + optional Splunk/Datadog webhook. Retention policy: configurable up to 7 years.
  * Data residency: full EU logical residency, proof for legal (signed DPA + subprocessor list).
  * Network diagram needed: subnets (private), recommended CIDR windows, NAT placements, route tables, security group examples, Transit Gateway options if multi-AZ peering.

-- PoC scope agreed (03/02/2026): 2-week lab deployment using customer VPC peering into Redwood Private control plane in eu-west-1. Traffic: chat front-end + reranker (peak 70 qps, p50 latency < 120ms). SE will provide initial terraform snippets.

-- Compliance & documentation requested: SOC2 snapshot, encryption-at-rest details, KMS keyflow diagram, sample audit log S3 lifecycle policy, security questionnaire (sent 02/15).

-- Quotes / commercial: Procurement asked for pricing deck and committed capacity options (dedicated pool for peak windows). AE shared price band; procurement requested a binding term sheet for 12-month committed capacity (requested by 03/10).

-- Internal notes: Jordan (SE) recommends PrivateLink for simplest customer allowlist posture; infra team prefers Transit Gateway for multi-account resilience. Need technical whiteboard to align.

-- Customer quote: 'we can't have ever-changing egress addresses—our partners will only accept fixed allowlists.' — Head of Infra.

-- Risks: Delay in legal DPA approval; potential additional effort to support BYOK HSM integration (customer uses CloudHSM FIPS modules).
